posts.title: JEE Physics Kinematics Notes: Formulas, Graphs, Projectile & Relative Motion
posts.excerpt: Complete Kinematics notes for JEE Main and Advanced: equations of motion, calculus method, motion graphs, projectile motion, river-boat and rain-umbrella problems, circular motion, common mistakes and a quick revision list.
posts.content:
Kinematics is the first chapter of JEE Physics and the base for everything that follows: laws of motion, work–energy, rotation and even electromagnetism use the same ideas of velocity, acceleration and relative motion. These notes cover the full JEE Main and Advanced syllabus for the chapter. Each section has the formulas, when to use them, and the traps examiners set.

> **How to use these notes:** read one section, then attempt the matching questions in the free [Kinematics chapter test](/jee/physics/kinematics-test). Come back to the "Common mistakes" list before every mock test.

## 1. Basic quantities

| Quantity / राशि | Type | Definition | SI unit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Distance / दूरी | Scalar | Total length of the path | m |
| Displacement / विस्थापन | Vector | Change in position, final − initial | m |
| Speed / चाल | Scalar | Distance ÷ time | m/s |
| Velocity / वेग | Vector | Displacement ÷ time, v = dx/dt | m/s |
| Acceleration / त्वरण | Vector | Rate of change of velocity, a = dv/dt | m/s² |

- Distance ≥ |displacement|. They are equal only for motion in one direction along a straight line.
- **Average speed** = total distance ÷ total time. **Average velocity** = total displacement ÷ total time.
- For two equal *distances* covered at speeds v₁ and v₂, average speed = 2v₁v₂/(v₁ + v₂) (harmonic mean). For two equal *time intervals*, it is (v₁ + v₂)/2.

## 2. Motion with constant acceleration

These four equations hold **only when acceleration is constant**:

1. v = u + at
2. s = ut + ½at²
3. v² = u² + 2as
4. sₙ = u + a(2n − 1)/2 (distance covered in the nth second)

Useful results:

- Starting from rest, distances in successive equal time intervals are in the ratio **1 : 3 : 5 : 7 …** (Galileo's law of odd numbers).
- Starting from rest, total distances after t, 2t, 3t … are in the ratio **1 : 4 : 9 …**.
- Stopping distance for a vehicle at speed u with retardation a: s = u²/2a. Doubling the speed makes the stopping distance **four times** as long.

## 3. Variable acceleration (calculus method)

When acceleration depends on time, velocity or position, the equations of Section 2 do **not** apply. Use calculus:

| Given | Use | Then |
|---|---|---|
| a = f(t) | a = dv/dt | v = ∫a dt, then x = ∫v dt |
| a = f(v) | a = dv/dt or a = v dv/dx | separate the variables and integrate |
| a = f(x) | a = v dv/dx | ∫v dv = ∫a dx |
| v = f(x) | a = v dv/dx | differentiate directly |

**Worked example.** a = −kv with initial velocity v₀. Using a = v dv/dx gives dv/dx = −k, so v = v₀ − kx. The particle stops after travelling **x = v₀/k**, even though the time taken is infinite.

## 4. Motion graphs

| Graph | Slope gives | Area under it gives |
|---|---|---|
| x–t (position–time) | Velocity | (no standard meaning) |
| v–t (velocity–time) | Acceleration | Displacement (signed area) |
| a–t (acceleration–time) | Jerk | Change in velocity |

- In an x–t graph, a straight line means uniform velocity and a curve means acceleration. Curving upward (concave up) means positive acceleration.
- In a v–t graph, area below the time axis is negative displacement. For **distance**, add the magnitudes of all the areas.
- A body cannot be at two positions at the same time, so an x–t graph can never curve back on itself in time.

## 5. Motion under gravity

Take **upward as positive** and g = −9.8 m/s² (or −10 m/s² if the question says so). Then the same equations work for the whole flight, both up and down.

- Thrown up with speed u: time to the top = u/g, maximum height = u²/2g, total time of flight = 2u/g.
- The speed on returning to the point of projection equals u (ignoring air resistance).
- Dropped from height h: time t = √(2h/g), and speed on reaching the ground v = √(2gh).
- A body thrown up from a height h reaches the ground at the positive root of −h = ut − ½gt².

## 6. Projectile motion

A projectile has **constant horizontal velocity** (u cos θ) and **uniform vertical acceleration** (−g). Treat the two directions separately.

| Quantity | Formula |
|---|---|
| Time of flight | T = 2u sin θ / g |
| Maximum height | H = u² sin²θ / 2g |
| Horizontal range | R = u² sin 2θ / g |
| Maximum range (θ = 45°) | R_max = u²/g, and then H = R_max/4 |
| Equation of the path | y = x tan θ − g x² / (2u² cos²θ) |
| Speed at the top | u cos θ (not zero) |

- Angles θ and (90° − θ) give the **same range**. Their heights satisfy **R = 4√(H₁H₂)**, and their times satisfy T₁T₂ = 2R/g.
- H = R when tan θ = 4. In general, tan θ = 4H/R.
- **Horizontal projection** from height h at speed u: time t = √(2h/g), range = u√(2h/g).
- Two projectiles launched at the same time see each other move in a **straight line**, because their relative acceleration is zero.

## 7. Relative motion

The velocity of A relative to B is **v_AB = v_A − v_B**.

- Same direction: speeds subtract. Opposite directions: speeds add.
- **Rain and umbrella:** find v_rain − v_man. Hold the umbrella opposite to that relative velocity. Rain at speed v_r and a man walking at v_m give tan θ = v_m / v_r with the vertical, with the umbrella tilted forward.
- **River crossing** (river width d, river speed v_r, swimmer speed v_s relative to the water):

| Goal | How to swim | Time | Drift |
|---|---|---|---|
| Minimum time | Straight across (perpendicular to the flow) | d / v_s | v_r · d / v_s |
| Shortest path (zero drift, needs v_s > v_r) | Upstream at sin α = v_r / v_s with the perpendicular | d / √(v_s² − v_r²) | 0 |

- **Meeting problems:** if two bodies have the same acceleration (for example both under gravity), use relative velocity directly. A ball dropped from height h and another thrown up at speed u at the same instant meet after **t = h/u**.

## 8. Circular motion (kinematics)

- Angular velocity ω = dθ/dt, and the relation v = ωr.
- **Centripetal acceleration** a_c = v²/r = ω²r, directed towards the centre. It changes only the direction of the velocity.
- **Tangential acceleration** a_t = dv/dt. It changes only the speed.
- Net acceleration a = √(a_c² + a_t²). In uniform circular motion a_t = 0, but the acceleration is **not** zero.

## 9. Common mistakes in JEE

1. Using s = ut + ½at² when the acceleration is not constant. Check first, and use calculus if a depends on t, v or x.
2. Reporting displacement when the question asks for distance. Find where v = 0 and split the motion at that point.
3. Mixing up sign conventions in vertical motion. Fix "up = +" once and keep g negative throughout.
4. Saying the velocity is zero at the top of a projectile's path. Only the vertical component is zero.
5. Writing v_BA as v_A − v_B. The velocity of B relative to A is **v_B − v_A**.
6. Forgetting to convert km/h to m/s (multiply by 5/18).
7. Using the "minimum time" and "shortest path" river formulas the wrong way round.

## 10. Quick revision: 10 facts to remember

1. The slope of x–t is v, the slope of v–t is a, and the area under v–t is displacement.
2. From rest, distances in equal intervals are in the ratio 1 : 3 : 5.
3. sₙ = u + a(2n − 1)/2.
4. Maximum height = u²/2g and time of flight (vertical throw) = 2u/g.
5. R = u² sin 2θ / g, maximum at 45°.
6. Complementary angles give the same range, and R = 4√(H₁H₂).
7. The speed at the top of the path is u cos θ.
8. v_AB = v_A − v_B.
9. Minimum-time crossing takes d / v_s. Zero-drift crossing takes d / √(v_s² − v_r²).
10. a_c = v²/r, a_t = dv/dt, and a_net = √(a_c² + a_t²).

**Next step:** attempt the free 30-question [Kinematics chapter test](/jee/physics/kinematics-test). It uses JEE Main marking (+4 / −1, 60 minutes) and shows the full solution to every question in English and Hindi.
